subproblems.title: Cofactor expansion det[p, e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}] = (−1)^j p_j (supplied step 6)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, p ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and j ∈ {0, …, n}. Let e_0, …, e_n be the standard basis of ℝ^{n+1} and let j.succAbove : {0, …, n−1} → {0, …, n} be the increasing enumeration of {0, …, n} ∖ {j} (j.succAbove k = k for k < j and k + 1 for k ≥ j). Let M be the (n+1)×(n+1) real matrix whose column 0 is p and whose column k+1 is e_{j.succAbove k} (k = 0, …, n−1); that is, M_{r,0} = p_r and M_{r,k+1} = (e_{j.succAbove k})_r, the r-th coordinate. Then det M = (−1)^j p_j, where p_j is the j-th coordinate of p.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : Euclid (n + 1)) (j : Fin (n + 1)), Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun r c : Fin (n + 1) => (Fin.cons p (fun k : Fin n => EuclideanSpace.single (j.succAbove k) (1 : ℝ)) : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)) c r) = (-1 : ℝ) ^ (j : ℕ) * p j
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 6 of the supplied proof of chart_perimeter: the expansion of det[φ(v), e_{j.succAbove 0}, …, e_{j.succAbove(n−1)}] along its first column (Matrix.det_succ_column_zero), "only the row-j term survives (every other minor contains the zero row j) and its minor is the identity". It is the coordinate form of the identity ω = Σ_j (−1)^{j−1} a_j dx^1 ∧ … ∧ \hat{dx^j} ∧ … ∧ dx^n of Simon Ch. 6, 2.34–2.35 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 594–595 and 625–626; 2.35 prints the sign as (−1)^j, a misprint, since dω = div a dx^1 ∧ … ∧ dx^n requires (−1)^{j−1} as in the proof of 2.34), written with indices counted from 0, where the sign becomes (−1)^j.

Proof.
1. (Entries.) By the definition of the standard basis vectors (EuclideanSpace.single; PiLp.single_apply), M_{r,0} = p_r, and M_{r,k+1} = 1 if r = j.succAbove k and M_{r,k+1} = 0 otherwise.
2. (Expansion along column 0.) By the Laplace expansion along the first column (Matrix.det_succ_column_zero), det M = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i M_{i,0} det N_i = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i p_i det N_i, where N_i is the n×n matrix obtained from M by deleting row i and column 0: (N_i)_{r,k} = M_{i.succAbove r, k+1}, which by step 1 equals 1 if i.succAbove r = j.succAbove k and 0 otherwise.
3. (The term i = j.) (N_j)_{r,k} = 1 if j.succAbove r = j.succAbove k and 0 otherwise. Since j.succAbove is injective, this is 1 if r = k and 0 otherwise. So N_j is the identity matrix and det N_j = 1 (Matrix.det_one).
4. (The terms i ≠ j.) Let i ≠ j. Since j ≠ i, j lies in the range of i.succAbove (Fin.exists_succAbove_eq): j = i.succAbove r₀ for some r₀ ∈ {0, …, n−1}. Row r₀ of N_i is (N_i)_{r₀,k} = [j = j.succAbove k], and j.succAbove k ≠ j for every k (Fin.succAbove_ne); so row r₀ of N_i is zero. A square matrix with a zero row has determinant 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero), hence det N_i = 0.
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–4, in the sum of step 2 only the term i = j is nonzero (Finset.sum_eq_single), so det M = (−1)^j p_j · 1 = (−1)^j p_j. ∎

```lean
  intro n p j
  rw [Matrix.det_succ_column_zero, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
  · -- the surviving term: the minor is the identity
    have hminor : ((Matrix.of fun r c : Fin (n + 1) => (Fin.cons p (fun k : Fin n => EuclideanSpace.single (j.succAbove k) (1 : ℝ)) : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)) c r).submatrix j.succAbove Fin.succ) = 1 := by
      ext r k
      simp [Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.one_apply, PiLp.single_apply]
    rw [hminor, Matrix.det_one]
    simp
  · intro i _ hij
    -- row `r₀` with `i.succAbove r₀ = j` of the minor vanishes
    obtain ⟨r₀, hr₀⟩ := Fin.exists_succAbove_eq (Ne.symm hij)
    have hzero : ((Matrix.of fun r c : Fin (n + 1) => (Fin.cons p (fun k : Fin n => EuclideanSpace.single (j.succAbove k) (1 : ℝ)) : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)) c r).submatrix i.succAbove Fin.succ).det = 0 := by
      apply Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero r₀
      intro k
      simp [Matrix.submatrix_apply, hr₀]
    rw [hzero, mul_zero]
  · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ j) h
```

N_j is the identity matrix because j.succAbove is injective.
For i ≠ j, writing j = i.succAbove r₀, row r₀ of N_i is zero, so det N_i = 0.
Hence det M = (−1)^j p_j.

subproblems.title: The determinant covector a ↦ det[p, Aa_0, …, Aa_{n−1}] as a continuous linear function of p (supplied step 4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let A : ℝ^P → ℝ^{n+1} be a continuous linear map. Then there is a continuous linear map Λ from ℝ^{n+1} into the space Λ^n(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P such that, for all p ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and a_0, …, a_{n−1} ∈ ℝ^P, Λ(p)(a_0, …, a_{n−1}) = det[p, Aa_0, …, Aa_{n−1}], the determinant of the (n+1)×(n+1) real matrix whose column 0 is p and whose column k+1 is Aa_k (entry (r, c) is the r-th coordinate of the c-th of the vectors p, Aa_0, …, Aa_{n−1}).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid (n + 1)), ∃ Λ : Euclid (n + 1) →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ (p : Euclid (n + 1)) (a : Fin n → Euclid P), Λ p a = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun r c : Fin (n + 1) => (Fin.cons p (fun k : Fin n => A (a k)) : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)) c r)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 4 of the supplied proof of chart_perimeter: "Λ(p)(a_0, …, a_{n−1}) := det[p, Aa_0, …, Aa_{n−1}] … is multilinear, alternating and continuous in (a_k), and p ↦ Λ(p) is linear". Here the continuity of p ↦ Λ(p) into Λ^n(ℝ^P) is made explicit, as it is needed for the smoothness of the test form.

Proof.
1. (The determinant form.) Let b be the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^{n+1} (EuclideanSpace.basisFun) and let D := det_b (Module.Basis.det of b.toBasis), the alternating (n+1)-linear form with D(v_0, …, v_n) = det(b.toMatrix v) (Module.Basis.det_apply). The matrix b.toMatrix v has entry (r, c) equal to the r-th coordinate of v_c (Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr). So D(v) is the determinant of the matrix with columns v_0, …, v_n.
2. (D is bounded.) Hadamard's inequality gives |D(v)| ≤ Π_i |v_i|. In Mathlib: for the orientation o := b.toBasis.orientation of ℝ^{n+1} (finrank ℝ^{n+1} = n + 1), Orientation.volumeForm_robust' gives |o.volumeForm v| = |D(v)|, and Orientation.abs_volumeForm_apply_le gives |o.volumeForm v| ≤ Π_i |v_i|. (Any bound |D(v)| ≤ c Π_i |v_i| would do; e.g. the Leibniz formula gives c = (n+1)!.) Hence AlternatingMap.mkContinuous with constant 1 turns D into a continuous alternating map D̄ with D̄(v) = D(v) for all v.
3. (Currying in the first slot.) ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft gives a continuous linear map D̄.curryLeft : ℝ^{n+1} → Λ^n(ℝ^{n+1}) with (D̄.curryLeft p)(w_0, …, w_{n−1}) = D̄(p, w_0, …, w_{n−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply; the tuple is Matrix.vecCons p w = Fin.cons p w).
4. (Pull-back by A.) The map ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM A : Λ^n(ℝ^{n+1}) → Λ^n(ℝ^P), g ↦ g(A·, …, A·), is continuous linear. Put Λ := (compContinuousLinearMapCLM A) ∘ D̄.curryLeft; it is a continuous linear map ℝ^{n+1} → Λ^n(ℝ^P).
5. (Values.) For p ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and a ∈ (ℝ^P)^n: Λ(p)(a) = (D̄.curryLeft p)(Aa_0, …, Aa_{n−1}) = D(Fin.cons p (A∘a)) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM_apply, compContinuousLinearMap_apply, curryLeft_apply_apply), and by step 1 this is the determinant of the matrix with column 0 equal to p and column k+1 equal to Aa_k. After rewriting with Module.Basis.det_apply, this matrix coincides definitionally with Matrix.of fun r c => (Fin.cons p (A∘a) c)_r, which is the asserted formula. ∎

```lean
  intro P n A
  set b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ with hb
  have : Fact (Module.finrank ℝ (Euclid (n + 1)) = n + 1) := ⟨by simp⟩
  -- Hadamard: |det v| ≤ ∏ ‖v i‖, so the determinant is a continuous alternating map
  have hbound : ∀ v : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1), ‖b.toBasis.det v‖ ≤ 1 * ∏ i, ‖v i‖ := by
    intro v
    rw [one_mul, Real.norm_eq_abs, ← Orientation.volumeForm_robust' (b.toBasis.orientation) b v]

  simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM_apply,
    ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply]
```

subproblems.title: Euclidean coefficient bound |α| ≤ (n+1)!·√(P^n) for the determinant covector (supplied step 8)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let A : ℝ^P → ℝ^{n+1} be a continuous linear map with operator norm ‖A‖ ≤ 1, let p ∈ ℝ^{n+1} with |p| ≤ 1, and let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) with α(a_0, …, a_{n−1}) = det[p, Aa_0, …, Aa_{n−1}] for all a_0, …, a_{n−1} ∈ ℝ^P (the determinant of the (n+1)×(n+1) matrix with column 0 equal to p and column k+1 equal to Aa_k). Then covectorEuclideanNorm(α) ≤ (n+1)!·√(P^n), where covectorEuclideanNorm(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} and e_0, …, e_{P−1} is the standard basis of ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid (n + 1)) (p : Euclid (n + 1)) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), ‖A‖ ≤ 1 → ‖p‖ ≤ 1 → (∀ a : Fin n → Euclid P, α a = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun r c : Fin (n + 1) => (Fin.cons p (fun k : Fin n => A (a k)) : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)) c r)) → covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ ((n + 1).factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt ((P : ℝ) ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 8 of the supplied proof of chart_perimeter ("every entry of M_w has absolute value ≤ 1 (|φ| ≤ 1 and |Ae_i| ≤ ‖A‖ ≤ 1), so |det M_w| ≤ (n+1)! (Matrix.det_le) … covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_φ(w)) ≤ (P^n((n+1)!)²)^{1/2} = c₀"). Departure (library gap only): Matrix.det_le lives in Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.AbsoluteValue, which is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission (#check Matrix.det_le: unknown constant), so step 1 below proves the same entrywise determinant bound from the Leibniz formula. The factor ζ(w) ∈ [0, 1] of the supplied proof is absorbed into p (test_form applies this lemma with p = ζ(w)φ(π(w)), |p| ≤ 1).

Proof.
1. (Leibniz bound.) Let m ∈ ℕ and let M be a real m×m matrix with |M_{r,c}| ≤ 1 for all r, c. By the Leibniz formula (Matrix.det_apply), det M = Σ_{σ ∈ Perm(Fin m)} sign(σ)·Π_i M_{σ(i), i}. By the triangle inequality (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs), |det M| ≤ Σ_σ |sign(σ)|·|Π_i M_{σ(i),i}|. Here sign(σ) = ±1 (Int.units_eq_one_or), so |sign(σ)| = 1, and |Π_i M_{σ(i),i}| = Π_i |M_{σ(i),i}| ≤ 1 (Finset.abs_prod, Finset.prod_le_one₀). Hence |det M| ≤ Σ_σ 1 = |Perm(Fin m)| = m! (Fintype.card_perm).
2. (Coefficients as determinants.) Fix I : Fin n → Fin P and write e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (the unit vectors of ℝ^P). By hypothesis α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) = det M^I, where M^I_{r,0} = p_r and M^I_{r,k+1} = (A e_{I(k)})_r.
3. (Entry bounds.) For a vector y ∈ ℝ^m and every coordinate r, |y_r| ≤ |y| (PiLp.norm_apply_le). Distinguish the column index (Fin.cases): for column 0, |M^I_{r,0}| = |p_r| ≤ |p| ≤ 1; for column k+1, |M^I_{r,k+1}| ≤ |A e_{I(k)}| ≤ ‖A‖·|e_{I(k)}| = ‖A‖ ≤ 1 (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm and |e_i| = 1).
4. (Each coefficient.) By steps 1–3 with m = n + 1, |α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})| ≤ (n+1)! for every I : Fin n → Fin P; hence α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})² ≤ ((n+1)!)² (sq_le_sq').

Source. Step 1 of the supplied proof of chart_perimeter ("Aι = id, ‖A‖ ≤ 1 (A is the adjoint of an isometry), and for v ∈ D, π(G(v)) = v, p^⊥(G(v)) = u(v) and A∘DG(v) = id (u and Du take values in (range ι)^⊥)"), with the omitted details filled in. Only differentiability of u on D is needed (the parent has u ∈ C²(D), which implies it).

Proof.
1. ((i) ‖A‖ ≤ 1.) Taking adjoints is a linear isometric equivalence between operator spaces (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint is a LinearIsometryEquiv; LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map), so ‖A‖ = ‖ι‖; and ‖ι‖ ≤ 1 because ι is a linear isometry (LinearIsometry.norm_toContinuousLinearMap_le).
2. ((ii) Aι = id.) For z, w ∈ ℝ^{n+1}: ⟨A(ιz), w⟩ = ⟨ιz, ιw⟩ = ⟨z, w⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left; LinearIsometry.inner_map_map). Since this holds for every w, A(ιz) = z (ext_inner_right).
3. (A kills u on D.) For v ∈ D and every w: ⟨A(u(v)), w⟩ = ⟨u(v), ιw⟩ = ⟨ιw, u(v)⟩ = 0 (adjoint_inner_left, real_inner_comm, hypothesis). Hence A(u(v)) = 0.
4. ((iii) and (iv).) Let v ∈ D. Then G(v) − x = ιv + u(v), so A(G(v) − x) = A(ιv) + A(u(v)) = v + 0 = v by steps 2–3, and therefore G(v) − x − ιA(G(v) − x) = ιv + u(v) − ιv = u(v).
5. (The derivative of G.) D is open and v ∈ D, so D is a neighbourhood of v and u is differentiable at v (DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt). By the sum rule (the constant x has derivative 0 and the continuous linear map ι is its own derivative), G has derivative ι + Du(v) at v, so DG(v) = ι + Du(v).
6. (A∘Du(v) = 0.) The map g := A∘u vanishes on the neighbourhood D of v (step 3), so g has derivative 0 at v (hasFDerivAt_const and HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). By the chain rule g also has derivative A∘Du(v) at v (A is continuous linear). By uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative (HasFDerivAt.unique), A∘Du(v) = 0.
7. ((v).) For y ∈ ℝ^{n+1}: A(DG(v)y) = A(ιy + Du(v)y) = A(ιy) + A(Du(v)y) = y + 0 = y by steps 2, 5 and 6. ∎

Notation. π(w) := A(w − x) and p^⊥(w) := w − x − ιπ(w) for w ∈ ℝ^P.

Proof.
1. (Chart identities.) By chart_geometry (u is differentiable on D and ⟨ιw, u(v)⟩ = 0 for v ∈ D): ‖A‖ ≤ 1, and for every v ∈ D, π(G(v)) = v, p^⊥(G(v)) = u(v) and A(DG(v)y) = y for all y. The maps π and p^⊥ are affine (continuous linear maps composed with w ↦ w − x), hence C^∞. Since w − x = ιπ(w) + p^⊥(w) and |ιπ(w)| = |π(w)| (ι is an isometry), |w − x| ≤ |π(w)| + |p^⊥(w)| for every w.
2. (Λ.) By det_covector applied to A there is a continuous linear map Λ : ℝ^{n+1} → Λ^n(ℝ^P) with Λ(q)(a_0, …, a_{n−1}) = det[q, Aa_0, …, Aa_{n−1}] (column 0 equal to q, column k+1 equal to Aa_k) for all q and a.
3. (Cut-off.) Put a := (δ₂/2)² and b := (3δ₂/4)²; since δ₂ > 0, b − a = 5δ₂²/16 > 0. Let ζ(w) := smoothTransition((b − |p^⊥(w)|²)/(b − a)), where Real.smoothTransition is C^∞ (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff), takes values in [0, 1], vanishes on (−∞, 0] and equals 1 on [1, ∞). ζ is C^∞, being smoothTransition composed with the C^∞ map w ↦ (b − |p^⊥(w)|²)/(b − a) (contDiff_norm_sq), and 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1.
  (3a) If ζ(w) ≠ 0, then (b − |p^⊥(w)|²)/(b − a) > 0 (otherwise ζ(w) = 0), so |p^⊥(w)|² < b and |p^⊥(w)| < 3δ₂/4.
  (3b) If |p^⊥(w)| < δ₂/2, then |p^⊥(w)|² < a, so (b − |p^⊥(w)|²)/(b − a) ≥ 1 and ζ(w) = 1.
4. (The form.) Define ω(w) := Λ(ζ(w)·φ(π(w))) for w ∈ ℝ^P. Then ω is C^∞: Λ is continuous linear, and w ↦ ζ(w)φ(π(w)) is C^∞ because ζ, φ and π are.
5. (Support.) Let S := {w : π(w) ∈ tsupport φ and |p^⊥(w)| ≤ 3δ₂/4}. S is closed, as an intersection of preimages of closed sets under the continuous maps π and |p^⊥|. If ω(w) ≠ 0 then ζ(w)φ(π(w)) ≠ 0 (because Λ(0) = 0), so ζ(w) ≠ 0 and φ(π(w)) ≠ 0; hence π(w) ∈ support φ ⊆ tsupport φ and, by (3a), |p^⊥(w)| < 3δ₂/4, i.e. w ∈ S. As S is closed, tsupport ω ⊆ S.
  (5a) (Compact support.) tsupport φ is compact, hence bounded: tsupport φ ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R. For w ∈ S, |w − x| ≤ |π(w)| + |p^⊥(w)| ≤ R + 3δ₂/4 by step 1. Thus tsupport ω is a closed subset of the compact ball closedBall(x, R + 3δ₂/4), so it is compact: ω has compact support.
